blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: To keep long interaction contexts tractable, stepwise group-relative training for multi-turn LLM agents materializes each source trajectory into multiple response rows and valid tokens. This expansion creates an outer-accounting problem distinct from within-trajectory credit assignment: row-based outcome statistics can count one episode outcome multiple times, while token-level reduction can assign unequal aggregate objective mass across trajectories. We term these effects outcome-statistics multiplicity and objective-mass imbalance. We introduce Outcome-Mass Alignment (OMA), a two-component method that makes both accounting choices explicit. Outcome Alignment computes outcome statistics over unique source trajectories, while Mass Alignment controls aggregate objective mass after within-trajectory aggregation of optimizer-native token objectives. Neither redesigns the base optimizer's credit assignment, importance ratios, or clipping. Across matched ALFWorld GRPO comparisons at two model scales, where failed trajectories typically expand much more than successful ones, OMA improves matched-horizon endpoint success by 7.0-9.4 percentage points. Ordinary WebShop exhibits weak or reversed expansion-outcome coupling and correspondingly mixed effects, whereas in a success-oriented WebShop setting, WebShop-SOL, OMA improves success nAUC from 0.399 to 0.511. Component ablations and GiGPO and GSPO comparisons further support component separability and cross-optimizer compatibility. These results show that trajectory expansion always defines an implicit weighting rule, but its practical effect depends on how expansion couples to outcomes and optimizer-native updates.
blocks.zh: 为使长期互动环境能够引导,针对多回合 LLM 代理的渐进组合相对培训将每个源轨迹变为多个响应行和有效符号。 这种扩展造成了一个不同于内置信用分配的外置会计问题:以行为基础的结果统计可以多次计算出一集结果,而象征性的降级则可以分配不同轨迹的不平等的总目标质量. 我们把这些影响称为结果统计的多重性和客观质量的不平衡。 我们采用成果-管理统一(OMA)这一两部分方法,使两种会计选择都明确。 结果对齐计算出相对于唯一源轨迹的结果统计,而质量对齐则在优化者-内在目标在轨集合后控制总目标质量。 既不重新设计基地优化者的信用分配、重要性比率,也不剪辑。 在两个模型尺度的ALFWorld GRPO比较中,失败的轨迹通常比成功的轨迹要大得多,而OMA则将匹配的视距终点成功率提高7.0-9.4个百分点。 普通的WebShop显示弱或逆转的扩展-结果耦合和相应的混合效果,而在面向成功的WebShop设置中,WebShop-SOL,OMA改进了成功的NAUC从0.399到0.511. 组件分解和GIGPO与GSPO的比较进一步支持组件分离性和跨优化兼容性。 这些结果表明,轨迹扩张总是定义了隐含的权重规则,但其实际效果取决于扩张伴侣对结果和优化本土更新的方式.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Large language models are increasingly used as agents that perceive, reason,
and act through repeated interaction with external environments. Representative
settings include embodied household tasks in ALFWorld ( Shridhar et al., 2021 ) and goal-directed web interaction in WebShop ( Yao et al., 2022 ) . These tasks require long-horizon planning under sparse
feedback: an agent may make tens of decisions before receiving a verifiable
episode-level outcome. Reinforcement learning is therefore a natural
post-training paradigm, and group-relative methods such as GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) offer a
scalable, critic-free way to learn from multiple attempts at the same task.
Extending this success to multi-turn agents,
however, requires deciding how a long environment interaction is presented to
the language-model optimizer.

blocks.en:
Multi-turn pipelines use two main materialization patterns. Trajectory-wise
optimization concatenates all states and model outputs into one sequence, as in
RAGEN ( Wang et al., 2025b ) , preserving full history but causing the effective
context to grow with the interaction horizon. Stepwise optimization instead
materializes each turn as a response row conditioned on a managed history,
keeping individual contexts tractable but expanding each source trajectory into
a variable number of optimizer-facing units
(Figure 1 (b)).

A direct stepwise adaptation of GRPO broadcasts the same trajectory-level
relative advantage to every row, obscuring which decisions helped or harmed.
GiGPO localizes credit through anchor-state groups ( Feng et al., 2025 ) , while
HGPO further organizes steps by historical-context consistency ( He et al., 2026 ) . These methods address which decisions receive credit within
a trajectory. Stepwise expansion, however, creates a separate outer-accounting
problem: after a source trajectory expands into multiple rows and tokens, how
much total statistical and optimization influence should it receive? OMA
targets this trajectory-level influence rather than redesigning
within-trajectory credit assignment.

Figure 1 illustrates how stepwise materialization can
reweight source trajectories: an ALFWorld task yields a 14-turn success with
1,663 response tokens and a 50-turn failure with
6,446 tokens, both sampled from the same policy checkpoint. Although each

outcomes with different multiplicities, while token-proportional reduction
assigns different aggregate objective mass

79.5% of the token-weighted objective mass. This expansion-induced
trajectory reweighting comprises outcome-statistics multiplicity and objective-mass imbalance . Stepwise materialization makes trajectory
influence depend implicitly on row and token expansion, without an explicit

blocks.en:
We introduce Outcome–Mass Alignment (OMA), an outer accounting
framework that makes these two choices explicit and controllable. Outcome
Alignment constructs the designated outcome statistics over unique source
trajectories before assigning the resulting learning signals to response rows.
Mass Alignment first aggregates the optimizer-native objective contributions
within each source trajectory and then controls its contribution to the outer
objective.
OMA therefore changes neither environment interaction nor the base optimizer’s
native within-trajectory credit, importance-ratio, and clipping mechanisms. Its
two components can be enabled independently or jointly and instantiated with
multiple group-relative policy optimizers.

blocks.en:
We evaluate OMA on ALFWorld and WebShop with GRPO, together with
GiGPO and GSPO adapter comparisons. ALFWorld exhibits strong success–failure
expansion asymmetry: across two model scales, OMA improves matched-horizon
success by 7.0–9.4 percentage points. Ordinary WebShop exhibits much weaker or
reversed expansion–outcome coupling and correspondingly mixed effects, whereas
a success-oriented WebShop setting, WebShop-SOL, improves success nAUC from
0.399 to 0.511. These results support a condition-dependent account: trajectory
expansion always defines an implicit weighting rule, but its practical effect
depends on how expansion couples to outcomes and optimizer-native updates.

blocks.en:
Policy optimization and objective aggregation. Language-model policy optimization builds on PPO ( Schulman et al., 2017 ) and critic-free estimators such as RLOO ( Ahmadian et al., 2024 ) . GRPO applies prompt-group relative advantages through
a clipped token surrogate ( Shao et al., 2024 ) ; DAPO modifies sampling,
clipping, and token aggregation ( Yu et al., 2025 ) ; Dr. GRPO removes
length and within-question variance scaling ( Liu et al., 2025 ) ; and
GSPO moves ratios and clipping to the sequence level ( Zheng et al., 2025 ) .
Related work balances token- and sequence-level contributions ( Zeng et al., 2026 ) , develops length-aware normalization or token
preferences ( He et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025a ) , and aligns off-policy
optimization with turn structure ( Li et al., 2026a ) ; broader comparisons study
interactions among estimators, environments, and rewards ( Wang and Ammanabrolu, 2025 ) . These methods modify normalization, credit,
gradient balance, or clipping within optimizer-facing units. OMA instead uses
source identity to define the outcome population and total outer objective mass
after row expansion.

Trajectory-length weighting. AsyncWebRL is the closest comparison on trajectory-length weighting ( Bai et al., 2026 ) . In multi-step GRPO, it replaces 1 / H i 1/H_{i} with a
trajectory-independent factor, making total weight proportional to H i H_{i} and
strengthening negative gradients from long failures to encourage efficient
termination. OMA neither prefers shorter trajectories nor scales mass with H i H_{i} : each source receives equal outer objective mass regardless of its row or

identities before broadcasting them to rows, removing representation
sensitivity. Both methods expose a length-dependent outer-mass design axis but

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
Stepwise multi-turn training expands one outcome into variable numbers of rows
and tokens, inducing outcome-statistics multiplicity and objective-mass
imbalance. OMA controls both through unique-trajectory statistics and equal
outer trajectory mass while preserving native credit, ratios, and clipping.

外轨质量,同时保留本土信用,比例和剪接.

blocks.en:
Results support a condition-dependent effect: OMA is most beneficial when
expansion couples strongly to outcomes and objective mass, as in ALFWorld,
where MA is strongest early–middle and full OMA late and at the endpoint.
Ordinary WebShop provides a weak or reversed boundary, while WebShop-SOL shows
sensitivity to outcome geometry. GiGPO and GSPO results suggest cross-optimizer
compatibility. Thus expansion defines an implicit trajectory-weighting policy.
